planMarkdown:
Bot: AnswerForge

Summary:
AnswerForge is a Telegram support automation agent that answers customer questions using company documentation and FAQs, escalates unresolved cases to humans, and continuously improves through feedback and knowledge-base updates.

Product goals:
Provide fast, accurate answers to common support questions directly in Telegram. Reduce repetitive support workload while keeping a smooth escalation path for complex or sensitive cases. Ground AI responses in approved docs and FAQs rather than open-ended generation. Track user satisfaction, unresolved questions, and knowledge gaps so the support team can improve documentation over time. Support a simple admin workflow for refreshing content, reviewing escalations, and monitoring bot health.

High-level architecture:
Run as a single Node.js ESM service using grammY for Telegram bot handling. The service receives Telegram updates via long polling or webhook, validates user/session context, and routes messages through a support-answer pipeline. The pipeline includes intent detection, retrieval of relevant knowledge-base chunks, AI answer generation with grounding constraints, confidence scoring, response formatting, and escalation handling. Documentation and FAQ content are ingested by an admin-only workflow: source files or text entries are parsed, normalized, split into chunks, embedded, and stored with metadata. MongoDB can store users, conversations, messages, knowledge documents, embeddings or vector-search-compatible records, feedback, and escalation tickets. If large files are uploaded, store the raw assets in generic object storage or filesystem storage and keep references in MongoDB. The AI provider integration should be isolated behind a service interface so models can be swapped without changing bot logic. Background jobs can run in the same process using scheduled tasks for re-indexing, cleanup, and analytics aggregation. No additional infrastructure such as Redis, Kafka, or SQL databases is required.

Data model:
Use MongoDB collections such as users, conversations, messages, knowledgesources, knowledgechunks, feedback, and escalations. users stores Telegram user ID, username, role, language preference, status, creation date, and last activity. conversations stores chat ID, user ID, current state, open escalation ID if any, and timestamps. messages stores user and bot messages, detected intent, retrieved chunk IDs, confidence, AI response metadata, and escalation status. knowledgesources stores uploaded documents, FAQ entries, URLs if supported, version, status, checksum, owner, and last indexed date. knowledgechunks stores source ID, chunk text, title/path, tags, language, embedding vector if supported by the selected MongoDB setup, revision, and visibility status. feedback stores message ID, rating, free-text comment, reason category, and reviewer state. escalations stores user ID, conversation ID, question, AI draft if generated, status, assigned admin if applicable, internal notes, and resolution summary.

Key flows:
Onboarding: /start introduces the bot, explains that answers come from official docs, and offers help commands. User support flow: the user asks a question, the bot normalizes the text, retrieves relevant FAQ/doc chunks, generates a concise grounded answer, includes references or source labels when available, and asks whether the answer helped. Low-confidence flow: if retrieval confidence is low, the bot asks a clarifying question or offers escalation. Escalation flow: unresolved issues create an escalation record, notify admins or mark the item for review, and tell the user that support will follow up. Feedback flow: users rate answers with helpful/not helpful actions; negative feedback is stored with the original question, answer, and sources for admin review. Knowledge ingestion flow: admins upload or register docs/FAQ content, the bot validates the file or text, chunks and embeds content, marks the new version active, and reports indexing results. Admin review flow: admins list unresolved questions, inspect failed answers, add missing FAQ entries, close escalations, and trigger re-indexing.

Tech stack:
Node.js with ESM as the runtime and application format. grammY for Telegram bot framework using TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN from environment variables. MongoDB for persistence, including users, sessions, conversations, knowledge content, feedback, and escalations. AI integration through a configurable LLM and embedding provider abstraction. Retrieval-augmented generation architecture using document chunking, embeddings, metadata filtering, and answer-generation prompts constrained to retrieved content. Use environment variables for configuration, structured logging for observability, and a validation library for input/config validation. File/image/document uploads should be stored in generic object storage or filesystem storage when needed, with MongoDB storing metadata and references.

Non-functional requirements:
Security: restrict admin commands by Telegram user ID allowlist or role stored in MongoDB, validate uploads, avoid exposing private docs, and never leak system prompts. Reliability: handle Telegram retries idempotently, store message processing metadata, and degrade gracefully when the AI provider is unavailable. Accuracy: require source-grounded answers, use confidence thresholds, display uncertainty, and escalate rather than hallucinate. Performance: cache recent knowledge lookups in process memory where safe, limit prompt size, chunk large documents efficiently, and apply rate limits per user. Privacy: store only necessary chat data, support data deletion workflows, and redact sensitive content in logs. Maintainability: separate modules for bot handlers, AI service, retrieval service, ingestion service, MongoDB repositories, admin workflows, and configuration. Operations: provide health checks, startup validation for TELEGRAMBOTTOKEN and database connectivity, structured logs, error alerts through logs or admin notifications, and safe graceful shutdown.

Bot commands:
• /start — Introduces the support agent and explains how to ask questions. (usage: /start) [user]
• /help — Shows available commands and explains how the bot uses docs and FAQs. (usage: /help) [user]
• /ask — Submits a support question explicitly, useful when the chat has other interactions. (usage: /ask How do I reset my password?) [user]
• /escalate — Creates a human-review escalation for the current issue. (usage: /escalate I still need help with billing) [user]
• /feedback — Sends feedback about the last answer. (usage: /feedback helpful or /feedback not helpful: missing pricing details) [user]
• /status — Shows whether the user has an open escalation or pending support request. (usage: /status) [user]
• /admin — Shows admin options for knowledge base, escalations, and system status. (usage: /admin) [admin]
• /uploaddocs — Admin-only command to upload or register documentation and FAQ content for indexing. (usage: /uploaddocs followed by a document attachment or text instructions) [admin]
• /reindex — Admin-only command to rebuild the searchable knowledge index. (usage: /reindex all or /reindex sourceid) [admin]
• /sources — Admin-only command to list indexed knowledge sources and their status. (usage: /sources) [admin]
• /unresolved — Admin-only command to list low-confidence questions, negative feedback, and open escalations. (usage: /unresolved) [admin]
• /close — Admin-only command to close an escalation with a resolution note. (usage: /close ESCALATIONID Resolved by sending account recovery steps) [admin]

envVarDocs.title: Telegram Bot Token
envVarDocs.description: Required token used by grammY to connect to Telegram.
envVarDocs.usage: Read in src/lib/config.js and required during boot.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Create a bot with BotFather on Telegram.

envVarDocs.title: MongoDB URI
envVarDocs.description: Stores users, messages, memory, knowledge docs, feedback, and escalations.
envVarDocs.usage: Used by src/lib/db.js. If missing, bounded in-memory fallback is used.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Create a MongoDB database and copy its connection string.

envVarDocs.title: CookMyBots AI Endpoint
envVarDocs.description: Base URL for the CookMyBots AI Gateway. Do not include /chat.

envVarDocs.title: CookMyBots AI Key
envVarDocs.description: Secret key for AI Gateway calls.
envVarDocs.usage: Sent as Authorization Bearer header by src/lib/ai.js.

envVarDocs.title: AI Timeout
envVarDocs.usage: Defaults to 600000 for slow AI responses.

envVarDocs.title: AI Max Retries
envVarDocs.description: Retry count for transient AI failures.

envVarDocs.title: General Concurrency
envVarDocs.description: Optional concurrency tuning value retained for runtime configuration.
envVarDocs.usage: Read by config with safe fallback.

envVarDocs.title: AI Model
envVarDocs.description: Optional model override passed to the AI Gateway.
envVarDocs.usage: If empty, the gateway default model is used.

envVarDocs.title: Admin User IDs
envVarDocs.description: Comma-separated Telegram numeric user IDs allowed to run admin commands.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Use Telegram user info tools or logs to find your numeric user ID.

envVarDocs.title: Support Confidence Threshold
envVarDocs.description: Minimum retrieval confidence before auto-escalation is created.

envVarDocs.title: Knowledge Top K
envVarDocs.description: Number of chunks retrieved per support question.

envVarDocs.title: Max Upload Bytes
envVarDocs.description: Maximum supported Telegram document size for /uploaddocs.

envVarDocs.title: Max Upload Characters
envVarDocs.description: Maximum text characters indexed from one upload.

envVarDocs.title: Global AI Cap
envVarDocs.description: Maximum simultaneous AI support jobs across the process.
envVarDocs.usage: Defaults to 1 for safe Render memory use.

envVarDocs.title: Runner Concurrency
envVarDocs.usage: Defaults to 1 for AI agent safety.
